 "summary": "Improves the connman fuzz target and FuzzedSock mock to more accurately simulate real operating system socket behavior and verify network handling invariants. It assigns unique descriptor values to each fuzzed socket to prevent cross-peer event collisions in CConnman::SocketHandler(). It also extends FuzzedSock::Wait() and WaitMany() to report partial events, error conditions, and connection resets.",
 "problem": "Fuzz testing of connman is unrealistic and misses real-world socket handling bugs. Every FuzzedSock previously recycled one of two descriptor values, causing SocketHandler() to merge entries and process one peer using another peer's socket events. In addition, FuzzedSock only returned either no events or exactly what was requested, leaving error paths and partial OS socket events unexercised.",
 "evidence": [

  "Commit 83392c75d2 notes that 'FuzzedSock::Wait() and WaitMany() reported either nothing or exactly the requested events. The real OS reports more than that, and the fuzz targets never exercised the callers on it.'"

<category name="tests" title="Test infrastructure">
## Covers

The machinery of testing rather than tests of a particular area: the
functional test framework and runner, unit test utilities, the fuzzing
harnesses and corpora, benchmarks, linters, sanitizer configuration,
and fixes for flaky tests whose cause is in the framework. A test that
pins the behavior of one area (a wallet migration test, a p2p relay
test) belongs to that area, not here. The Tests and Fuzzing labels are
a prior, but a labeled PR whose tests are about one area goes to that
area instead.

## What matters here

Signal first: fixes for flaky or misleading tests, since a red CI that
nobody trusts hides real failures. Then coverage of high-risk code paths
that the fuzzers or functional tests do not reach, especially
consensus, mempool policy, and p2p message handling. Then framework
capabilities that unblock tests other areas need. Then test speed, which
every contributor pays for on every run. Then cleanliness of the test
code.

Adding tests for their own sake ranks low; adding a test that catches a
realistic regression ranks high.
